title: Your weekly trade review is missing a step

channel.name: Andrew Builds (TradeNotes)
channel.appBlurb: a trading journal and performance analytics app

body.hook: Your weekly trade review is missing a step. Probably the important one.
body.promise: Before: reread trades, feel bad. After: a ten-minute loop. Its last step gets skipped.

beats.narration: Step one: find the leak. Sort the week by tag, pick the habit that shows up most.
Step two: question the fix. Backtest a rule that would have blocked it. That shows history, not the future.

scene.label: Step 2: rule to test
scene.text: No new trade for 30 minutes after a loss.
scene.caption: History, not a prediction.

beats.narration: Most reviews stop there. Step three, the skipped one: write the rule where you'll see it before Monday's first trade.
Why does that matter? Next week's review starts with one count: the days you followed it.
I built TradeNotes, my own trading journal, so I'm biased. It keeps tags and notes in one place for that review.
So the journal finds the leak, the backtest questions the fix, and the written rule closes it. None of it removes the risk of loss.

body.cta: Set a ten-minute timer this weekend, and run the loop once. Not financial advice.

promise.sub: Ten minutes. The last step gets skipped.

post.ytTitle: Your weekly trade review is missing a step
post.ytDesc: A ten-minute weekly loop: the journal finds the leak, a backtest questions the fix, and you write the rule down before Monday. A backtest shows what a rule did historically (hypothetical, not a prediction), the dot count on screen is SAMPLE data, and nothing here removes the risk of loss. I built TradeNotes, so I'm biased. Part 5 of 5. Educational content only, not financial advice.
